item.title: Iran declares Argentine Navy Air Force terrorist organizations
item.description: In response to the Argentine government’s hostile move, contrary to the fundamental principles of international law, in designating the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC), one of the official components of the Islamic Republic of Iran’s Armed Forces, as a terrorist entity, the Government of the Islamic Republic of Iran, in accordance with the principle of reciprocity and pursuant to the 2019 Law on Reciprocal Action in Response to the United States’ Designation of the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps as a Terrorist Organization, hereby declares the Argentine Navy and Argentine Air Force subject to the provisions of the aforementioned law and designates them as terrorist organizations. The law stipulates that: “All countries that in any way comply with or support the decision of the United States of America to designate the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps as a terrorist organization shall be subject to reciprocal action.” It is self-evident that the Argentine government shall bear responsibility for all consequences arising from this action.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran has categorically rejected the French government's baseless and malicious accusations against Iran over alleged involvement in cyber activities in France, strongly condemning the French government's discredited policy of making accusations against Iran. The latest accusations against Iran, which follow a series of repeated allegations and claims aimed at diverting public attention from France's destructive policies toward Iran and the West Asian region, particularly its decades-long hosting of terrorist groups and support for the genocide of Palestinians, constitute an extremely irresponsible and despicable attempt to tarnish Iran's image and undermine its relations with other countries. Such actions serve only to please the United States and the Israeli regime, the world's biggest violators of international law. The French government's baseless allegations amount to an attempt to deflect attention from its own governance failures, its inability to meet the people's demands, and its failure to address shortcomings in the country's management systems. These are shortcomings so severe that the French authorities are even unable to control the temperature of refrigerators, yet seek to shift the blame onto foreign actors by making despicable accusations. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly advises French officials to spend their resources on addressing the livelihood and educational needs of their own people, rather than allocating huge budgets to interfere in other countries, including through the abuse of diplomatic cover and ostensibly cultural projects. The Islamic Republic of Iran, while reminding the French government of its international responsibility for actions that violate international law and France's illegal interventions against Iran, emphasizes that it will not hesitate to take the necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security against unlawful foreign activities.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran reaffirms Iran’s principled position in condemning the violation of Yemen’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity. The continued aggression against Yemen’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity, together with the economic and aerial blockade of the country, is contrary to international law and Islamic teachings. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns, in particular, the airstrikes on civilian infrastructure and non-civilian areas. These include the airstrikes of 6 November on the Al-Hadara public market in Al-Waza’iyah district, Taiz Governorate, Yemen, which resulted in the martyrdom of 33 innocent Yemenis, including 13 innocent children, and the wounding of dozens of others; the airstrikes on Al-Shariyah village in Bani Hashish district, east of Sana’a Governorate, which resulted in the martyrdom of 33 people, including several children and women; and the targeting of members of the media team of Yemen’s Al-Masirah network while they were engaged in journalistic activities. These attacks are not only a clear violation of Article 2, paragraph 4 of the Charter of the United Nations, but also a flagrant breach of the fundamental principles of international humanitarian law and constitute a war crime. The Islamic Republic of Iran notes that the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen must be brought to an end as soon as possible through dialogue between the parties on the basis of the agreed roadmap between them. This requires the immediate cessation of military attacks, the complete lifting of the blockade, and respect for the right of the Yemeni people to self-determination.

item.title: Iranian Tunisian foreign ministers hold phone talks
